articles.title: THE XIAOMI 18 FOLD LEAKS, AHEAD OF THE IPHONE ULTRA LAUNCH
articles.summary: The smartphone industry appears to be coalescing around the book-style foldable design, where a phone unfolds into a small tablet, rather than the flip-phone format that folds a standard phone in half. Samsung's latest Galaxy Z Fold, Apple's rumored iPhone Ultra, and leaked images of Xiaomi's upcoming 18 Fold all point to growing momentum behind larger-screen foldables, suggesting that this form factor is emerging as the preferred direction for premium folding phones.

articles.title: ADOBE BRINGS ACR'S POWERFUL NON-DESTRUCTIVE EXPOSURE TOOLS INTO PHOTOSHOP ITSELF
articles.summary: Adobe has released a major Photoshop update focused on making image editing faster and more intuitive, with new features including a Light Adjustment Layer that brings Camera Raw-style lighting controls directly into Photoshop, Firefly-powered editing tools that can automatically mask and modify specific parts of an image from text instructions, and AI Markup tools for visually communicating edit requests. The update also introduces a beta AI-Assisted Editor, allowing users to make complex edits through natural-language prompts while Photoshop automatically selects and combines the appropriate tools. Adobe says the goal is to let creators spend less time navigating software and more time focusing on creative decisions.

articles.title: GAMMA ACQUIRES ACCEL-BACKED DESIGN STARTUP LICA
articles.summary: Presentation startup Gamma has acquired Accel-backed Lica to build a design research lab, which Lica's co-founders will lead. Lica raised $4 million in 2024 and worked with e-commerce sites on brand-compliant marketing videos. Gamma now wants to explore fluid, multimodal presentation formats through the new division.

articles.title: THE CREATIVITY WE OUTSOURCE — AI, CREATIVITY AND THE LOST VALUE OF DOING THINGS YOURSELF
articles.summary: Generative AI can deliver a solution before there is time to explore the problem, removing the detours where creative learning actually happens. Photoshop began stripping away that friction. AI takes it much further, especially for students and young designers. The proposal is not banning AI but designing for Learning Experience alongside User Experience.

articles.title: SPEAKING DESIGN AT SCALE
articles.summary: Design system pattern names like Overview and PageHeader are shorthand for decisions a team should not have to reopen every time. Learning that vocabulary takes a person months, but an agent can read the repository and retrieve the code, guidance, and examples behind each name. That lets more people describe a screen in the system's own language and judge the result.

articles.title: THE PRODUCT DESIGNER'S ROLE ISN'T DISAPPEARING. IT'S GETTING WEIRDER
articles.summary: AI is collapsing the traditional boundaries between product design, product management, and engineering, making the old handoff-based workflow increasingly obsolete. As AI tools can now turn ideas, requirements, and design systems into working prototypes and code, designers are being pushed toward a broader role the author calls a product architect—someone who combines product thinking, systems design, technical understanding, and creative judgment. Rather than focusing on screens, specs, or deliverables, the most valuable skill becomes deciding what should be built, how it should work, and whether it solves a real problem. This can be an opportunity rather than a threat: design isn't disappearing, but evolving into a more strategic, multidisciplinary role where taste, judgment, and systems thinking matter more than execution.

articles.title: A FREE STOCK PHOTOGRAPHY COLLECTION LED BY DISABLED CREATIVES
articles.summary: A free stock photography collection led by disabled creatives to help marketers, advertisers, and creative teams tell more authentic stories about disability.

articles.title: AI-NATIVE CREATIVE PLATFORM
articles.summary: Every top AI image, video, and audio model on one infinite canvas. Storyboard, iterate, and publish templates — or open a focused generator for a single shot.

articles.title: ANIMATION IS HAVING A PUNK ROCK MOMENT – AND IT SAYS A LOT ABOUT HOW PEOPLE VIEW AI
articles.summary: Niu Lai, a nearly zero-budget animated film made largely by a Chinese mother and son on second-hand computers, has become an unexpected box office hit. Made by former interior designer Xin Yumeng over five years, the crude, low-quality animation grossed over ¥25.67 million despite starting with almost no publicity or earnings. Its success is framed as a reaction against polished, AI-generated visuals, echoing how punk rock once rebelled against overproduced music.

articles.title: PERFECTION IS NOT OVER-ENGINEERING
articles.summary: Over-engineering means solving the wrong problem, not caring too much, or building something too good. With every constraint on the table, only one solution fits, and that solution is the perfect one. Over-engineering is therefore a failure of requirements gathering, and systems need treating as products with real users.

articles.title: THE CBI'S LATEST AI REPORT ON HOW DESIGN BUSINESSES CAN BRIDGE AI'S EXECUTION DIVIDE
articles.summary: The real value of AI now comes from integrating it into core business operations rather than running isolated experiments. Design teams benefit most when AI supports entire workflows from concept creation to production. AI's biggest near-term impact is augmenting human work rather than replacing it, making skills like judgment, creativity, and critical thinking even more important. Automation is reducing traditional entry-level design tasks, creating a risk to the future talent pipeline unless companies redesign junior roles around AI-assisted workflows while also addressing growing legal and copyright concerns around AI-generated work.

articles.title: CREATIVE CLARITY
articles.summary: Creative confusion stalls work, while clarity comes from breaking the process into phases and knowing which one is current.

articles.title: THE INFINITE SCROLL WAS A DESIGN CRIME. NOW META IS PAYING FOR IT
articles.summary: State attorneys general are arguing in a federal trial that Meta's endless feed was engineered to break human willpower.
